findings.reason: the dependency list is the only gate that holds §10 until its upstreams land; six missing edges let the measurement run early and read as a fleet that never took the repair.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` lists §10's waits through s50 only, while s51–s56 each change how a landing is measured, refused or recorded and are all recorded implementable, so a dispatch of §10 on the declared graph could measure a fleet that has not taken six of the landing repairs it is meant to measure

findings.reason: the followup is the dispatch instruction a coordinator reads; dropping six implementable sections ends the chain early and leaves the plan looking finished.
findings.text: the one open followup `f-dwl-s50` names "sections 46 to 50 … and the live-fleet day in section 10" while the declarations at plan.html:23 record s51–s56 implementable, so the chain a coordinator follows drops six sections before the measurement

findings.reason: a control that cannot fail at base leaves the node with no way to show its guard fires, which is the rubric's own bar for done-when.
findings.text: §55's negative control says the base case fails "with a close comment written or the pointer removed", but at base promotion raises every refusal before the comment is written (`_landing_gate` runs inside `_require_independently` at promotion.py:1489, and the comment is written after that block at promotion.py:3372), and the pointer is retired only after `ledger.append_run` (promotion.py:3408), so the case passes at base and the control cannot be produced

findings.reason: if the three writes are already ordered after the refusals, the stated cause is another path (the comment names a second plan, inverse-equilibrium-baseline, which a concurrent landing could have closed), and a node repairing the ordering the plan names would fix nothing.
findings.text: §55 states that after a replay refusal "the lander nonetheless wrote a c-close-s9 comment … set that plan's §9 declaration to done, and removed the run's live pointer", but the base ordering has the gate replay raise before `_record_comment_with_snapshot` (promotion.py:1489, 3372) and the pointer retired only through `_release_integrated_pointer`, which refuses unless the head is integrated (`landed_workspace_refusal`, pending_landing.py:192-243); nothing on the refusal path in `_land` writes the beat (`queue_landing.py:3017` writes it only when `accepted`)

findings.reason: an endpoint with no reachable input cannot be built or tested, so the third case must either be dropped or the plan must state which partitions carry a maximum and where that fact comes from.
findings.text: §54 requires that "a declared duration longer than any partition admits is refused at declaration, naming the longest limit available", but the system holds no partition maximum: `partition_for_bound` (landing_measure.py:877-892) knows only a one-hour debug window and a long partition defaulted to `rigel`, which carries no limit, so with the default routing no duration can exceed every maximum and the refusal has no input that triggers it

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §55's declared negative control asserts a base failure (a close comment written or the pointer removed on a refused replay) that the base code path does not produce, so the case cannot redden at base.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — each node writes its base and head gate logs under its own run directory and never to a scratchpad.

rubric_items.reasoning: findings — §54's third case names a partition-maximum fact the system does not hold. §55's root cause is not the ordering the base code has.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of s54, s55 and s56 names one deliverable and one verdict closes it.
